titleEn: Stop at the Door and Say Hello!

pages.text: A spring morning. The yard gate stood wide open. "Hello, Duri!" Teacher Bau of Rainbow Class greeted at the gate. Careless Duri rushed past, neckerchief fluttering.
"Rainbow Class has a new picture book. I want to see it first!" Duri ran toward the shoe rack without once looking at who stood by the gate.
A mail carrier stood there with a paper parcel. "Wait, this—" he called, but Duri was far away already. Behind Duri, the classroom door clicked shut.
Duri searched up and down the classroom bookshelf. No new picture book anywhere. "Oh? It is not here?" Duri tugged the neckerchief knot.
"Duri, the mail carrier called you," Teacher Bau said, holding the parcel. "He was waiting to place it in your hands." From the yard gate, Duri saw him already at the road's end.
Teacher Bau knelt before Duri. "Duri, try stopping your feet at the door. Stop at the door and say hello! Then you can see who is there."
The next morning, Duri stopped before the threshold. Both feet stood side by side. Duri looked up. "Stop at the door and say hello!"
Teacher Bau stood at the door. "Hello, Teacher!" Beside Teacher Bau stood the mail carrier. "Hello!" He placed a paper parcel in Duri's hands.
Duri tapped the threshold with toes and recited, "One, feet stop at the door! Two, look up! Three, say hello!" That day, Duri stopped at the classroom door too and looked at Teacher Bau.

Teacher Bau rubbed a nose against Duri's forehead. "Stopping to look let you see the mail carrier, right?" Stop your feet at the door, and you see whom to greet. Hugging the parcel, Duri waved. "Stop at the door and say hello!"
